previous_admission_summary.summary_paragraph: A male patient with a history of SIADH, hypertension, aortic stenosis, and chronic bilateral rotator cuff tears was admitted after being struck in the head with a ball during physical therapy. He reported transient visual changes but had no headache or neurological deficits. Initial labs revealed acute hyponatremia (Na 121) and acute renal failure (creatinine 1.5), likely due to poor oral intake and accidental low-salt diet. A non-contrast head CT showed no acute intracranial injury. He received one liter of normal saline, which improved sodium to 127 and creatinine to 1.0. His blood pressure was managed with continued home antihypertensives. He remained stable, with no complications, and was discharged to an extended care facility on a revised medication list including ranitidine for GI protection and continued management of chronic conditions.
problems: Other accident caused by striking against or being struck accidentally by objects or persons
